rows.grounds: locative plural indicating placement in the cardinal directions
compound tatpuruṣa-ādīn with enclitic ca; accusative plural object
locative plural indicating placement in the intermediate corners
compound hṛdaya-ādi-aṇūn; accusative plural object; aṇu taken here as subtle mantra-form in ritual context

items.question: Which mantra forms are assigned to the cardinal directions and which to the intermediate corners?
premises: The cardinal directions are specified as locations for placement.
Tatpuruṣa and the other related forms are assigned to the directions.
The intermediate corners are specified as distinct locations.
The heart and other related subtle forms are assigned to the corners.
items.inference: Tatpuruṣa and the other associated forms are placed in the cardinal directions, while the heart and other associated subtle forms are placed in the intermediate corners.
uncertainties: The exact referents of ādi in tatpuruṣādīn and hṛdayādya are not explicitly enumerated in this verse.
The sense of aṇūn as subtle mantra-forms rather than individual selves is inferred from the ritual placement context.
items.plain_english: In the directions one should place Tatpuruṣa and the others, and in the corners the Heart and the other subtle forms.
